summary: The exact candidate adds a useful opt-in Python controller skeleton and passes its focused tests, but an independent CPU and GPU adversarial case shows that reused_prediction() exposes the cached last-real tensor directly. An in-place scheduler/consumer mutation corrupts subsequent reuse, violating the core last-real-prediction contract. The work is also framework-only and has no qualified model adapter or end-to-end stateful diffusion validation.
remaining_counterexamples: A scheduler or other consumer mutating a reused model_output in place changes StepReuseState.last_real_prediction; the next skipped step returns the mutated tensor rather than the last real prediction. Reproduced on CPU and AMD Instinct MI355X.

No concrete model adapter is enabled, so request/modality/CFG scope switching, observation semantics, thresholds, forced persistent writes, and quality gates are not validated on a real stateful diffusion architecture.
Real multi-rank decision agreement and collective-control-flow safety remain unverified with only one assigned GPU.
Model-specific _run_denoising_step overrides that bypass the shared implementation do not receive reuse behavior without further integration.

remaining_limitations: No native rebuild was applicable: the candidate changes only Python and tests, and the prepared environment records native=null.
No qualified diffusion model weights or architecture adapter were available; the deterministic tiny Llama fixture is not applicable to diffusion quality or stateful world-model semantics.
Only one GPU was assigned, so real TP/SP/CFG-parallel broadcast behavior was not executed.
The candidate's previously recorded MI350X claim was not treated as independent proof; this review's visible assigned device identified as AMD Instinct MI355X.
